## Source
.design/m5/49-hardware-token-signing.md — operator docs.

## Surface
- New file: `docs/operations/hardware-token-signing.md`
- Sections:
  1. Hardware support matrix (PKCS#11 HSMs, YubiKey PIV, FIDO2)
  2. Token initialization (one-time setup per token)
  3. Mode selection (attended-batch vs attended-realtime)
  4. PIN management (where applicable; security discipline)
  5. Touch-per-sign workflow
  6. `polaris labeler-sign-pending` daily operations (batch mode)
  7. `polaris-signer` daemon ops (realtime mode): TLS setup, cert pinning, monitoring
  8. Rotation: PKCS#11 (full destroy supported) vs FIDO2 (credential management via authenticator UI)
  9. Token-loss recovery (rotate to a replacement token; old key in revoked_keys; emitted labels still verify)
  10. Troubleshooting (PIN failures, touch timeouts, daemon disconnect)

## Rust-quality notes
- Per rust-quality §8: every CLI invocation copy-pasteable; one runnable example per section.
- The docs explicitly contrast PKCS#11 vs FIDO2 trade-offs so operators choose well.

## External references
- v1 ops runbook (style reference): `docs/ops/runbook.md`
- YubiKey PIV documentation: https://developers.yubico.com/PIV/
- softhsm2 setup (for testing): https://github.com/opendnssec/SoftHSMv2

## Acceptance
- [ ] `docs/operations/hardware-token-signing.md` exists; ≥300 lines; covers all 10 sections.
- [ ] CI markdown-lint passes.
